findings.title: Migration crashes when no legacy embed category is configured
findings.body: The category lookup is indexed immediately with `[0]['id']`. On a normal installation where `embed_category` was left at its default, is absent from `site_settings`, or no longer matches a category name, the query returns no rows and this raises on nil before the fallback at lines 14-16 can run. This prevents the entire database migration from completing; both legacy-setting lookups need to handle an empty result and use the uncategorized fallback safely.

findings.title: Legacy URL-form allowed hosts are migrated into unusable records
findings.body: This raw INSERT copies each legacy setting value verbatim, bypassing `EmbeddableHost`'s normalization callback. The previous setting accepted entries such as `https://example.com/path`, but the new authorization lookup parses a referer to `example.com` and queries `lower(host) = 'example.com'`; it will not match the stored URL/path. Upgrading such an existing configuration silently disables embedding for every URL-form host until each row is manually edited. Normalize the legacy values before inserting them (or create records through the model).

findings.title: Duplicate host rows make the selected category ambiguous
findings.body: There is no uniqueness validation or database constraint on `host`, while this lookup returns only the first row matching `lower(host)`. Admins can create duplicate or case-variant entries for the same domain with different categories through the new UI; only one of those categories will be used for imports, and editing the other row has no predictable effect on routing. Canonicalize hosts and enforce a case-insensitive unique host mapping, or otherwise define deterministic multi-row behavior.

findings.title: Hosts containing a port are accepted but can never authorize embeds
findings.body: The validation permits values such as `example.com:3000`, and the normalization callback preserves the port. `URI(host).host` deliberately strips that port, however, so this query searches for `example.com` while the database contains `example.com:3000`. Consequently any host entered with a port is displayed as saved but all requests from it are rejected. The stored and lookup forms need to treat ports consistently (for example, strip/reject ports on save or compare URI authority).

findings.title: Removing all allowed hosts no longer disables expansion of existing embeds
findings.body: `expandable_first_post?` no longer checks whether any embeddable host is configured. With `embed_truncate` enabled, an old topic with a `TopicEmbed` remains expandable even after every host has been removed; expansion fetches the historical remote URL through `TopicEmbed.expanded_for`. This defeats the prior disable switch and can keep server-side remote fetches/content from a deliberately removed host available. Replace the removed setting check with an appropriate `EmbeddableHost` existence/authorization check.

findings.title: A newly saved uncategorized host is shown without its server-assigned category
findings.body: When a new host is saved with no category selected, the server assigns `uncategorized_category_id`, but `categoryId` is still null in this component. The success handler then explicitly replaces the host's category with `Discourse.Category.findById(null)`, discarding the category represented by the response. The row therefore shows no category until a reload and subsequent edits continue to submit a blank selection. Set `categoryId` from the returned `host.category_id` and resolve that value instead.

findings.title: Updating or deleting an already removed host produces a server error
findings.body: Both `update` and `destroy` use `where(...).first` and immediately dereference the result. If another administrator has deleted the row, or the client sends a stale/nonexistent id, `save_host(nil)` calls `host.host` and `destroy` calls `nil.destroy`, producing a 500 instead of a not-found response. This is a normal concurrent-admin workflow for this UI; handle a missing record explicitly before saving or destroying.
